title: prospectorQualtrics Dashboard
text:
When to run it:
While the schedule says, “if I am alive, I will run a check for new responses every X minutes”, the actual execution of the job is determined by SCRONTAB. This instead says, “wake up this process every Y time of day by running this script.”
To add this to SCRONTAB, paste the code generated by cronR to your SCRONTAB file:

library(cronR)
library(here) # makes it easier to deal with path issues

here() starts at /n/holylabs/cgolden_lab/Lab/frontier/works/prospectors/prospectorQualtrics

cmd <- cron_rscript(
  here("run.R"), 
  workdir = here(),
  rscript_log = here("pipelines/logs/orchestrator.log"),
  log_append = TRUE,
  log_timestamp = TRUE
)
cron_cmd <- cron_add(command = cmd, frequency = 'daily', at = "09:00", id = 'prospectorQualtrics', dry_run=TRUE, ask=FALSE)

Adding cronjob:
---------------

## id:   prospectorQualtrics

With some SCRONTAB config we’ll need:

library(glue)
mail_user <- Sys.getenv("SLACK_EMAIL")
runtime <- Sys.time()
git_cmd <- "git commit -a -m 'cron job commit @ {runtime}' && git push"
glue(
'#SCRON -J Maestro-prospectorQualtrics', 
'#SCRON -p hsph', 
'#SCRON --mem=1G', 
'#SCRON -t 00:10:00', 
'#SCRON --mail-type=FAIL,END', 
'#SCRON --mail-user={mail_user}', 
'{cron_cmd$min} {cron_cmd$hour} {cron_cmd$day_of_month} {cron_cmd$month} {cron_cmd$day_of_week} {cron_cmd$command} && {git_cmd}',
.sep = "\n")

title: Process Qualtrics Data Uploads
text: This prospector is designed to dynamically fetch and ingest data from our Qualtrics survey projects.

title: Process Qualtrics Data Uploads
text:
Setup

library(dplyr)


Attaching package: 'dplyr'


The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':

    filter, lag


The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

library(glue)
library(qualtRics)
library(googlesheets4)
library(here)

here() starts at /n/holylabs/cgolden_lab/Lab/frontier/works/prospectors/prospectorQualtrics


We first need to access the Qualtrics API to retrieve any new data:

print("Setting up Qualtrics API connection...")

[1] "Setting up Qualtrics API connection..."

connection_to_api <- "Connected"

We can access the exact Qualtrics project that has all of our data upload records using its ID:

print("Accessing Qualtrics project...")

[1] "Accessing Qualtrics project..."

qualtrics_project_id <- "1234567890"
print(paste("Project ID:", qualtrics_project_id))

[1] "Project ID: 1234567890"

survey_df <- data.frame(
  respondent_id = c("R1", "R2", "R3"),
  response = c("Yes", "No", "Yes"),
  data_gt_50mb = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE),
  data_path_globus = c(NA, NA, "globus://path/to/large/data/R3")
)
print("Survey data retrieved:")

[1] "Survey data retrieved:"


We should also get the corresponding google sheet that tracks whether or not the response has been processed:

gsheet <- "url to google sheet"
sheet_df <- data.frame(
  respondent_id = c("R1", "R2", "R3"),
  processed = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)
)

title: Process Qualtrics Data Uploads
text:
Processing
We process a response by checking whether the data is expected to be larger than 50mb; if not, we can directly download it to the gold_mine qualtrics folder from the qualtrics response object ID:

sheet_df |>
    filter(!processed) |>
    left_join(survey_df, by = "respondent_id") |>
    rowwise() |>
    mutate(
        download_path = ifelse(data_gt_50mb == FALSE, paste0("gold_mine/qualtrics/", respondent_id, ".csv"), data_path_globus)
    ) |>
    ungroup() -> unprocessed_responses


print("Unprocessed responses with download paths:")

[1] "Unprocessed responses with download paths:"

print(unprocessed_responses)

# A tibble: 3 × 6
  respondent_id processed response data_gt_50mb data_path_globus   download_path
  <chr>         <lgl>     <chr>    <lgl>        <chr>              <chr>        
1 R1            FALSE     Yes      FALSE        <NA>               gold_mine/qu…
2 R2            FALSE     No       FALSE        <NA>               gold_mine/qu…
3 R3            FALSE     Yes      TRUE         globus://path/to/… globus://pat…


For responses with data larger than 50mb, we can use the globus path to download the data to the gold_mine qualtrics folder, and for responses with data smaller than 50mb, we can directly download it from the qualtrics response object ID to the gold_mine qualtrics folder. We can use a global function called download_data that takes in the download path and the respondent ID to handle both cases:

download_data <- function(download_path, respondent_id) {
    if (grepl("globus://", download_path)) {
        print(paste("Downloading large data for respondent", respondent_id, "from globus path:", download_path))
        # Code to download from globus would go here
    } else {
        print(paste("Downloading small data for respondent", respondent_id, "from Qualtrics response object ID:", download_path))
        # Code to download from Qualtrics would go here
    }
}

unprocessed_responses |>
    rowwise() |>
    mutate(
        download_result = download_data(download_path, respondent_id)
    ) -> processed_responses

[1] "Downloading small data for respondent R1 from Qualtrics response object ID: gold_mine/qualtrics/R1.csv"
[1] "Downloading small data for respondent R2 from Qualtrics response object ID: gold_mine/qualtrics/R2.csv"
[1] "Downloading large data for respondent R3 from globus path: globus://path/to/large/data/R3"


And after processing, we must update the google sheet to mark the response as processed:

updated_sheet_df <- sheet_df |>
    left_join(processed_responses, by = "respondent_id") |>
    mutate(processed = ifelse(!is.na(download_result), TRUE, FALSE))

This pipeline will be run on a regular schedule, so technically this counts as a dynamic daily ETL pipeline, so it should be run with maestro and SCRONTAB. See this notebook for more details on how this was set up: SCRONTAB Jobs with Maestro.

title: Orchestrating The Maestro Job with SCRONTAB
text:
This is a scrontab job that runs every 15 minutes to check for new responses in the google sheet and process them accordingly. The job is set up using maestro and SCRONTAB, which allows us to schedule and automate the execution of this pipeline.
library(maestro)
library(glue)
library(cronR)
library(here)

here() starts at /n/holylabs/cgolden_lab/Lab/frontier/works/prospectors/prospectorQualtrics
We created the job scaffold using create_maestro:

title: Orchestrating The Maestro Job with SCRONTAB
text:
What to run
This chunk sets up the pipelines for a maestro cronjob. maestro recognizes the special comments in the function definition to determine the schedule and logging behavior of the job.

Process Data

#' Ferry Qualtrics Responses To The Gold Mine
#'
#' @maestroFrequency 1 hour
#' @maestroStartTime 2026-06-12
#' @maestroTz US/Eastern
#' @maestroLogLevel INFO
process_data_pipeline <- function() {

  print("Running the maestro pipeline...")
  source(here("R/process_qualtrics_data.R"))

}

This function will be executed according to the schedule defined in the comments. The content of this routine can be viewed in the Process Qualtrics Data Uploads notebook.
